context: The input is an ascending array of 10 distinct elements at indices 0 through 9. The search target is 6 (target = 6). The input table gives the value at each index.

Pointers i and j mark the left and right boundaries of the current closed search interval [i, j], which includes both endpoints. The midpoint index m is (i + j) / 2 rounded down. Each iteration first computes m, then compares nums[m] with the target.
description: The seven frames show initialization followed by three comparisons. Each iteration has one frame for computing the midpoint and another for narrowing the interval or finding a match. A dashed outline marks the current search interval.

frames.announcement: Set the left boundary i to index 0 and the right boundary j to index 9 to search the entire array.
frames.explanation: Set i = 0 and j = 9. The closed search interval [0, 9] covers all 10 elements, with 1 at the left endpoint and 35 at the right. The midpoint m has yet to be computed.
frames.key_state: i = 0 and j = 9. The closed search interval is [0, 9]. There is no midpoint m yet.
frames.title: Initialize the search interval

frames.announcement: The midpoint index m is 4. Its value, 12, is ready to be compared with the target, 6.
frames.explanation: In the closed interval [0, 9], i = 0 and j = 9. Rounding m = (0 + 9) / 2 down gives 4, the index of 12. Next, compare 12 with the target, 6.
frames.key_state: i = 0, j = 9, and m = 4. The midpoint value is 12. Next, compare it with the target, 6.
frames.title: Iteration 1: Compute midpoint m = 4

frames.announcement: The midpoint value 12 is greater than the target, 6. Move the right boundary j to index 3, keeping indices 0 through 3.
frames.explanation: In the original interval [0, 9], the value 12 at m = 4 is greater than the target, 6. Since the array is in ascending order, the target cannot be at index 4 or to its right. Set j = m - 1 = 3. Now i = 0 and j = 3. The interval [0, 3] contains [1, 3, 6, 8]. The old midpoint pointer m still points outside the interval to index 4 (value 12) until the midpoint is recomputed.
frames.key_state: The value 12 at m = 4 is greater than the target, 6, so the interval shrinks from [0, 9] to [0, 3]. Now i = 0 and j = 3, leaving [1, 3, 6, 8]. The old midpoint m = 4 is outside the interval.
frames.title: Iteration 1: 12 is greater than 6, so move the right boundary to 3

frames.announcement: Recomputing the midpoint m in [0, 3] gives index 1, whose value is 3.
frames.explanation: In the closed interval [0, 3], i = 0 and j = 3. Rounding m = (0 + 3) / 2 down gives 1, the index of 3. Next, compare 3 with the target, 6.
frames.key_state: i = 0, j = 3, and m = 1. The midpoint value is 3. Next, compare it with the target, 6.
frames.title: Iteration 2: Compute midpoint m = 1

frames.announcement: The midpoint value 3 is less than the target, 6. Move the left boundary i to index 2. Only 6 and 8 remain in the interval.
frames.explanation: In the original interval [0, 3], the value 3 at m = 1 is less than the target, 6. Since the array is in ascending order, the target cannot be at index 1 or to its left. Set i = m + 1 = 2. Now i = 2 and j = 3. The interval [2, 3] contains [6, 8]. The old midpoint pointer m still points outside the interval to index 1 (value 3) until the midpoint is recomputed.
frames.key_state: The value 3 at m = 1 is less than the target, 6, so the interval shrinks from [0, 3] to [2, 3]. Now i = 2 and j = 3, leaving [6, 8]. The old midpoint m = 1 is outside the interval.
frames.title: Iteration 2: 3 is less than 6, so move the left boundary to 2

frames.announcement: Recomputing the midpoint m gives index 2, the same index as the left boundary i. Its value is 6.
frames.explanation: In the closed interval [2, 3], i = 2 and j = 3. Rounding m = (2 + 3) / 2 down gives 2. The midpoint now coincides with the left boundary i and points to 6. Next, compare this value with the target, 6.
frames.key_state: Both i and m are at index 2, and j = 3. The midpoint value is 6. Next, compare it with the target, 6.
frames.title: Iteration 3: Compute midpoint m = 2

frames.announcement: The midpoint value equals the target, 6. The search succeeds and returns index 2.
frames.explanation: The value 6 at m = 2 equals the target, 6, so the search ends. The final frame shows only the midpoint pointer m at index 2. The boundary pointers i and j and the dashed outline are hidden.
frames.key_state: Found the target value 6. Only m = 2 is visible. Return index 2.
frames.title: Iteration 3: Target found, return index 2

result: The midpoint values are 12, 3, and 6, in that order. The third comparison finds 6 and returns its index, 2.
summary: Search an ascending array for 6. In each iteration, compare the midpoint element with the target and rule out the half that cannot contain it.
title: Binary search
